data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is less resilient than a highly redundant monolith when the 'independence' of the small services is illusory, masking shared dependencies on a common infrastructure layer (e.g., a specific cloud provider's DNS or a common OS kernel bug).","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services utilize diverse underlying infrastructure (multi-cloud, diverse OSes).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The monolith's internal redundancy is perfectly homogeneous, making it susceptible to a single software bug that affects all redundant nodes simultaneously.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The failure mode is 'latent synchronization': independent operators unknowingly utilize the same underlying substrate, transforming a decentralized logical topology into a centralized physical topology, thereby inheriting the monolith's failure risk without its coordinated redundancy management.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
